verified_facts: a legal boundary is an exact line with no thickness or width
a physical boundary can differ from the legal boundary
Ordnance Survey mapping does not show the legal boundary itself
most registered titles use the general boundaries rule
title-plan red edging is a reasonable interpretation rather than an exact survey line
there is no standard tolerance measurement or ratio between a general boundary and legal boundary
physical boundary survey accuracy does not create title-boundary exactness
general-boundary geometry must not be promoted to centimetre precision
quality_effect: Prevents general-boundary map lines from being treated as exact legal boundaries or assigned an invented tolerance.
